Title: Order number alone opens tracking and the final file when the account has no phone
Description: The public tracking endpoint and the anonymous final-document gate compared the supplied phone with the stored one without requiring either to be non-empty.
Reproduction: Customer clears their phone in the profile (allowed). Anonymous GET /api/orders/track/?order_number=KH-2026-000001&phone= returns 200; GET /api/documents/<id>/download/?order_number=KH-2026-000001&phone= returns the file. Order numbers are sequential.
Root_Cause: Missing-parameter and blank-value cases not rejected; phone is an optional profile field.
Impact: Unauthorized disclosure of order status and final result for any account without a phone.
Verification: Both values are mandatory and non-blank on both endpoints; anonymous download gate shares the 10/min tracking throttle. 3 tests.
Residual_Risk: A phone number remains a weak second secret for accounts that have one; signed links would be stronger.

Title: Customer can mark their own upload as the final result
Description: The customer upload endpoint accepted is_final_document and verification_note from the request body, and any document_type including FINAL_RESULT.
Reproduction: Customer POST /api/customer/orders/<id>/documents/ with is_final_document=true, verification_note='approved by manager'. The stored document is flagged final and appears as the final result in public tracking.
Root_Cause: One serializer shared by customer, provider and staff uploads; server-owned fields were passed through.
Impact: Forged final result on the customer's own order; misleading tracking output; staff could verify a customer file as the result.
Verification: Customer uploads always store is_final_document=False and an empty review note; type must be one of the order's requirements and never FINAL_RESULT. 2 tests.

Title: Unverified and rejected final results are visible and downloadable by the customer and public tracking
Description: As soon as a provider uploaded a result it was listed and downloadable by the customer and through the public gate, before staff verification, and remained so after staff rejected it.
Reproduction: Provider uploads result (order READY_FOR_DELIVERY). Customer detail lists it, download returns 200, public tracking lists it. Staff rejects it: still listed and downloadable.
Root_Cause: No visibility rule for final documents; ownership was the only check.
Impact: A wrong file (possibly another person's document) reaches the customer before the review step that exists to catch it. PRD journey: verify and complete, then download.
Verification: One rule (documents.services.is_customer_visible_document): a final result is customer material only when the order is completed and the file is not rejected. Applied to customer detail, download, token issue, tracking and the public gate. 3 tests; browser journey still downloads after completion.
Residual_Risk: Providers and staff still see the file, as intended.

Title: Previous provider organization keeps access after reassignment; cross-organization reassignment fails; inactive membership grants access
Description: Reassigning an order to a provider without an organization left the previous provider's organization on the order, so its members kept access. Reassigning to a provider in another organization raised a validation error. The provider portal query ignored membership is_active.
Reproduction: Order assigned to provider A (org A), returned to review, assigned to provider B. A colleague in org A still gets 200 on /api/provider/orders/<id>/. With B in org B the assign call returns 400. A deactivated org member still opens the order.
Root_Cause: assign_provider never cleared assigned_provider_organization; two copies of the provider visibility query.
Impact: Provider can read an order and its documents after losing the assignment.
Verification: Assignment always sets the organization from the new provider (or clears it); both provider queries require an active, non-deleted membership. 3 tests.

Title: Internal transition reasons and staff identity are sent to the customer and to public tracking
Description: The status timeline returned every status-log note plus changed_by id and name to the order owner and to anonymous tracking.
Reproduction: Staff returns a result to the provider with reason 'INTERNAL-ONLY provider invoice dispute'. Customer detail and GET /api/orders/track/ both contain the text and the staff member's name and user id.
Root_Cause: One timeline serializer for all audiences.
Impact: Internal remarks and staff names disclosed to customers and to anyone holding order number and phone. SRS: internal notes are hidden from customers.
Verification: Customer and public timelines use a serializer without staff identity; a note is included only for transitions written for the customer (waiting for customer, rejected, cancelled). Staff view unchanged. 5 tests.
Residual_Risk: Providers still receive all status notes of their assigned order.

Title: A late customer upload silently undoes approved readiness and blocks the provider
Description: Customers could upload to any open order. A new unreviewed file became the latest for its type, so readiness turned incomplete and the provider's result upload and completion were refused.
Reproduction: Order IN_PROGRESS with approved documents. Customer uploads national_id again (201). Provider result upload now returns 400 'Required documents are incomplete'.
Root_Cause: Upload permission tied to 'not closed' instead of the intake stage.
Impact: Customer can stall an order by accident; staff outside the review queue cannot easily repair it.
Verification: Customer uploads are accepted in NEW, UNDER_REVIEW and WAITING_CUSTOMER only; the UI flag follows the same set. 2 tests.

Title: Workflow actions run on stale data without a lock and are not atomic
Description: No workflow action locked the order row or reloaded it. Two requests prepared against the same state both succeeded and wrote contradictory status, timeline and assignment rows. Several actions wrote status, timeline, notification and audit rows outside one transaction.
Reproduction: Load the order twice. Reject through the first copy, then assign a provider through the second: the rejected order becomes ASSIGNED with both timeline rows. Force the notification step to fail during assignment: status and timeline are already saved.
Root_Cause: Read-validate-write on an in-memory instance with a full-row save; no select_for_update; multi-step writes not wrapped.
Impact: Status, timeline, assignment and notifications can contradict each other under double clicks, two tabs or two staff members.
Verification: orders/locking.py: every workflow service and document review runs in one transaction holding a row lock and re-reads the order first; refused attempts are still audited after rollback. 4 tests.
Residual_Risk: None known. A two-thread race on PostgreSQL 16 is now part of the suite (config/tests_hardening_closure.py::ConcurrentWorkflowRaceTests) and passes: exactly one decision wins, one timeline row, one notification.

Title: Documents of closed orders can still be approved or rejected
Description: The review endpoint did not check the order state.
Reproduction: Cancel an order, then POST /api/staff/documents/<id>/verify/: 200. Reject the verified final result of a completed order: 200, the order stays COMPLETED with a rejected result.
Root_Cause: Missing state precondition.
Impact: History of a closed order can be rewritten; completed order left without a valid result.
Verification: Review of a deleted document or of a closed order's document is refused. 2 tests.

Title: Catalog edits change the requirements of existing orders
Description: Readiness, uploads, document requests and labels all read the live catalog. Adding a required document to a service blocked every in-flight order of that service; removing one erased it from existing orders, including a pending missing-document request.
Reproduction: Order IN_PROGRESS. Admin adds a required document to the service: provider result upload returns 400. Admin removes the requirement of an order under review: its readiness shows no documents and the customer's requested document disappears from the upload page.
Root_Cause: No per-order copy of the requirements.
Impact: Silent corruption of in-flight and historical orders by routine catalog maintenance.
Verification: Order.requirements_snapshot is frozen at creation and is the only source for readiness, uploads, requests, provider file access and labels. Migration orders.0015 adds the column; orders.0016 backfills existing orders in committed batches. 4 tests; migration rehearsed on SQLite (legacy copy) and PostgreSQL 16 (20,008 orders).
Residual_Risk: Legacy snapshot assumption: orders that existed before the migration are frozen with the catalog as it is on migration day. No source can reconstruct earlier rules (requirement rows have no timestamps and rule changes were not audited). `manage.py audit_requirements_snapshot` lists the orders where this is visible.

Title: A retry that loses the race gets a validation error instead of the original order
Description: When two requests with the same key overlapped, the loser could fail in model validation of the unique constraint, which was returned as HTTP 400. Only the database IntegrityError path was handled.
Reproduction: First request commits between the second request's pre-check and its save. Second request returns 400 'Order with this Customer and Submission key already exists'.
Root_Cause: full_clean validates unique constraints before the insert.
Impact: No duplicate order, but a legitimate retry is shown an error although the order exists.
Verification: Both failure shapes re-check the key and return the original order (200) or 409 for a different payload. 3 tests plus the browser retry spec.
Residual_Risk: Requests without an Idempotency-Key are not de-duplicated (documented API contract).

Title: An organization administrator can make themselves a platform super admin
Description: Membership roles were writable without restriction through two endpoints. The platform-role check ignored the organization type and the model rule tying roles to organization types never ran. The per-user permissions endpoint let the same actor grant any Django permission to themselves.
Reproduction: As a partner admin: POST /api/organization-memberships/ {user: self, organization: own, role: 'platform_super_admin'} returns 201 and the account passes every admin check. Same through POST/PATCH /api/admin/users/ with membership_role. PATCH /api/admin/users/<self>/permissions/ with ['payment.refund_payment','auth.add_permission'] returns 200. Memberships in other organizations were accepted too.
Root_Cause: No authority check on who may assign which role where; selector trusted the role name alone.
Impact: Full platform takeover by any organization-level administrator.
Verification: One rule (assert_can_assign_membership) on both endpoints; platform roles count only on the platform organization and cannot be stored elsewhere; permission changes are super-admin only and limited to the application allowlist. 7 tests.
Residual_Risk: Exploitable only by an account that already holds an organization-admin role.

Title: Restore actions ignore scope and the delete guard
Description: Fifteen restore actions loaded the record with Model.objects.get(pk) instead of the scoped queryset.
Reproduction: Partner admin POST /api/admin/users/<any id>/restore/ reactivates a deleted or banned user of another organization. An unknown id returns HTTP 500.
Root_Cause: Custom action bypassed get_queryset; delete was guarded, its inverse was not.
Impact: Cross-tenant reactivation of users, memberships, branches, services and providers.
Verification: Restore is limited to the same actors as delete (platform super admin) in the shared mixin; unknown ids return 404. 2 tests.

Title: Soft-delete fields are writable through PATCH
Description: is_deleted, deleted_at and delete_reason were ordinary writable fields on user, service, organization and other admin serializers.
Reproduction: PATCH /api/admin/users/<id>/ {is_deleted: true} deletes the user without the delete password, super-admin check or delete audit entry.
Root_Cause: Fields listed in serializers without read-only protection.
Impact: Bypass of the delete guard and its audit trail.
Verification: Soft-delete fields are read-only in every model serializer through one mixin. 1 test over three record types.

Title: Replacing a user's password does not end their existing sessions
Description: Admin-set passwords (users and providers) did not bump the token version, so access and refresh tokens issued before the change kept working.
Reproduction: Employee logs in. Admin changes the employee's password. The old access token still returns 200 on /api/auth/me/ and the old refresh token still mints new ones for up to 7 days.
Root_Cause: token_version was bumped only by self-service reset and logout-all.
Impact: A compromised account stays compromised after the administrator resets it.
Verification: Both admin password paths bump token_version. 5 session tests (password change, deactivation, role change, logout, anonymous).

Title: The notification centre shows and changes other people's notifications
Description: For admin, employee and provider the bell listed notifications addressed to other users, counted them as unread, and 'mark all as read' marked them read for their real recipients.
Reproduction: Customer has unread notifications. Admin (or the assigned provider) opens the bell and presses 'mark all as read'. The customer's notifications are now read; the customer never saw them. The list also exposes recipient email and phone.
Root_Cause: The personal notification centre reused an oversight query scoped by order.
Impact: Customers miss missing-document and completion notices; cross-user disclosure of contact details.
Verification: List, unread count, mark-read and mark-all-read are limited to the recipient for every role. Staff oversight stays on the admin notification log. 3 tests plus browser check.

Title: Providers receive customer identity, prices and revenue through the reports summary
Description: GET /api/reports/summary/ returned, for a provider, the full order list projection (customer name, phone, email, national id, final price) and revenue and payment totals.
Reproduction: Provider with one completed order calls /api/reports/summary/: response contains the customer's phone, email, final_price, revenue per category/branch and payment_summary.
Root_Cause: Report helpers used the staff order serializer and finance aggregates for every role.
Impact: Violates SRS: provider cannot access finance reports; customer personal data disclosed beyond the provider projection.
Verification: Providers get the provider order projection and no revenue or payment figures. 1 test with 6 assertions.

Title: Unpublished services can be ordered by id; related services leak another partner's private services
Description: Order creation accepted any active service id, including services hidden from the public site or in hidden categories. The service page's related list was filtered by category only.
Reproduction: Set show_on_public_site=False on a service (or move it to a hidden category). POST /api/orders/ with its id returns 201.
Root_Cause: Creation used a weaker filter than the catalog.
Impact: Draft or withdrawn services receive real orders.
Verification: Order creation requires the service to be visible in the customer's catalog; related services follow catalog scope. Existing orders of a later unpublished service keep working. 5 tests.

Title: Reading the public homepage re-publishes unpublished content
Description: When no content was marked active, the public GET picked the latest row, set it active and served it.
Reproduction: Admin unpublishes the homepage content. The next anonymous GET /api/public-site/homepage/ shows it and flips active_content back to true.
Root_Cause: 'Get or create active' helper shared by the public view and the editor.
Impact: Draft is not distinguishable from published; unpublish does not work.
Verification: Public read never writes publish state; unpublished content is replaced by built-in defaults. Editor loads the latest version. 1 test plus browser CMS spec.
Residual_Risk: There is still a single content version, not a separate draft.

Title: An organization administrator can change platform-wide records
Description: Organization-scoped administrators could create global services, move services between organizations, edit document rules and provider links of any service, read every customer address, edit platform system settings including the published contact details, change the password and email of shared provider accounts, and write branches, branding and service configuration of other organizations.
Reproduction: As partner admin: POST /api/admin/services/ without organization creates a public global service; PATCH /api/admin/service-documents/<id>/ {provider_can_view_file: true}; POST /api/admin/system-settings/ {key:'site.contact'}; PATCH /api/admin/providers/<id>/?order=1 {password, email}.
Root_Cause: Permission classes admit organization admins; querysets and foreign keys were not limited to their organization.
Impact: Cross-tenant tampering, phishing through contact details, provider account takeover.
Verification: Platform-owned records refuse writes from organization-scoped users; services are limited to the actor's own organization; organization foreign keys are validated; provider identity and approval are super-admin only; system settings are admin only. 3 tests.
Residual_Risk: Category management keeps its existing organization scoping and was not changed.

Title: Demo seed with published credentials can run on a live system
Description: seed_demo and seed_initial_data --include-demo-users created or updated fixed-password accounts including a superuser with no environment check.
Reproduction: Run python manage.py seed_demo with DJANGO_DEBUG=False: admin@khalisni.local / published password exists as superuser.
Root_Cause: No guard.
Impact: Accidental creation of a known-password superuser on production.
Verification: Both commands refuse demo users and orders unless DEBUG is on or --allow-non-debug is passed deliberately. Startup never runs them. 1 test.
Residual_Risk: The older global Order.objects.exists() guard still only skips demo orders; it does not rewrite real data.

Title: Customer payment records accept refund type, non-positive amounts and gateway fields
Description: The customer payment endpoint accepted payment_type=refund, amount 0, and client-supplied gateway name and URL.
Reproduction: Customer POST /api/customer/payments/ {payment_type:'refund', amount:'5.00'} returns 201.
Root_Cause: Server-owned fields exposed on the payer serializer.
Impact: Misleading finance records.
Verification: Refund type and non-positive amounts are refused; gateway fields are read-only for customers. 2 tests.
Residual_Risk: Amount is not compared with the order price (fee semantics are undecided, B10-8). Payment status changes have no state machine.

Title: Registration ignores the password policy; login and registration have no dedicated rate limit
Description: Registration accepted '12345678'. Login was limited only by the general anonymous rate (120/min).
Reproduction: POST /api/auth/register/ with password 12345678 returns 201. Forty wrong logins in a row all return 401.
Root_Cause: validate_password not called at registration; no throttle scope.
Impact: Weak passwords and faster password guessing.
Verification: Registration and admin-set passwords use the configured validators; login 20/min and registration 20/hour per client (env-tunable). 3 tests.
Residual_Risk: See KHS-033 for how the client address is derived behind proxies.

Title: Fee components are sent to customers and providers regardless of the service's visibility settings
Description: Order payloads embedded service_fee and government_fee for every role, although the service marks them as not public.
Reproduction: Service with show_government_fee_public=False. Provider's /api/reports/summary/ and customer order detail include government_fee.
Root_Cause: Order's service summary ignored the visibility flags.
Impact: Fee breakdown disclosed against the configured setting.
Verification: Outside the operations team the two components follow the service's visibility flags. No fee rule was changed.
Residual_Risk: Fee meaning remains a client decision (B10-8).

Title: Customer order page shows a spinner forever when the order cannot be loaded
Description: The page ignored the load error. Provider and admin dashboards had the same pattern.
Reproduction: Open /customer/orders/<id of another customer's order> from an old link or notification: endless spinner.
Root_Cause: error from the data hook never read.
Impact: User cannot tell what happened or what to do next.
Verification: The three pages show the server's reason and a way back. Lint, 69 unit tests and browser route suite pass.

Title: Missing-documents resubmission dead-ends after a partial failure
Description: Files were uploaded one by one with no record of which succeeded. After one failure, a retry re-sent the first file, the server refused the duplicate, and the remaining files were never reached.
Reproduction: Two documents requested. First uploads, second is rejected. Fix the second and resubmit: error on the first, stuck until manual refresh.
Root_Cause: No per-file state.
Impact: Customer cannot complete the requested correction.
Verification: Already-uploaded types are skipped on retry and the error is attached to the file that failed. Existing page test and browser journey pass.

Title: A remembered login in another tab silently replaces the account under a live session
Description: Stored tokens in localStorage took priority over the tab's own session, and no tab listened for storage changes.
Reproduction: Tab A signed in as customer A. Tab B signs in as B with 'remember me'. Tab A still shows A but sends B's token; an order submitted in tab A is created under B with A's prefilled data.
Root_Cause: Storage priority and no storage listener.
Impact: Order created under the wrong account with another person's details.
Verification: A tab keeps its own session; tabs sharing a remembered login reload when it changes. 2 unit tests.
Residual_Risk: Tokens remain in web storage (readable by any injected script).

Title: After a refused action the screen keeps showing actions that are no longer valid
Description: Employee, provider and admin order pages showed the error toast but did not refetch.
Reproduction: Two staff members open the same order. One rejects it. The other presses assign: toast shown, page still offers assign.
Root_Cause: No refetch on failure.
Impact: Repeated failing actions and confusion about the real state.
Verification: Pages refetch when the server refuses an action for a state reason; field validation errors keep the typed input. 2 unit tests.

Title: A 409 on resubmission silently discards the key and allows a second order
Description: On a key conflict the wizard dropped the key and showed a raw English message; the next click created a new order.
Reproduction: Submit times out but succeeds on the server. Customer edits a field and resubmits (409), then clicks again: second order.
Root_Cause: Conflict treated as a new submission.
Impact: Duplicate logical order after a timeout.
Verification: The customer is told a request may already exist and to check their requests before sending again. Browser idempotency specs pass on desktop and mobile.
Residual_Risk: A customer who ignores the message can still deliberately submit again.

Title: Internal document type codes and three untranslated strings on customer screens
Description: The document list printed document_type codes; three notification-panel keys were missing from both locale files.
Reproduction: Customer order page shows 'national_id' under the file name; English bell shows Arabic 'mark all as read'.
Root_Cause: Code used as label; missing keys.
Impact: Raw identifiers in customer UI.
Verification: Customers see the configured document name; keys added to both locale files.
Residual_Risk: See KHS-037.

Title: nginx request body limit is below a normal multi-document request
Description: client_max_body_size was 10m while each document may be 10 MB and one request carries several.
Reproduction: Create a request with two 6 MB documents through nginx: 413 from nginx before Django.
Root_Cause: Limit sized for one file.
Impact: Order creation fails with an unhelpful error for larger uploads.
Verification: Raised to 50m. Configuration validated with `nginx -t` in the project's nginx:1.27-alpine image and exercised end to end through the container (journey 8/8).
Residual_Risk: Not yet deployed.

Title: Empty provider notes accepted; completed-orders counter updated non-atomically
Description: Provider note endpoint stored whitespace-only notes; the counter used read-modify-write.
Reproduction: POST /api/provider/orders/<id>/notes/ {note:'   '} returns 201.
Root_Cause: Missing validation.
Impact: Noise in the audit trail; miscount under concurrency.
Verification: Empty notes return 400; counter uses an F() update. 1 test.

Title: The request-form schema of a service is stored without validation
Description: Any JSON was accepted as required_information_schema.
Reproduction: PATCH /api/admin/services/<id>/ {required_information_schema: {key:'x'}} returns 200; the customer form silently loses its fields.
Root_Cause: JSON field with no validator.
Impact: Customer form silently drops or merges fields.
Verification: Structure, unique keys, labels, type and options are validated on save. All 311 existing imported fields already satisfy the rule. 2 tests.
Residual_Risk: Field semantics remain a client decision (B10-1/2).

Title: Rate limits are keyed on a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For and counted per worker
Description: nginx appends the client's own X-Forwarded-For and DRF used the whole header as identity. The password-reset limit used the left-most (caller-written) entry and the audit log stored the proxy's address. Compose did not pass the throttle, JWT or reset variables to the backend at all. Without Redis the counters are per gunicorn worker.
Reproduction: Send each login attempt with a different X-Forwarded-For value: each gets a fresh budget (if the edge proxy passes the header through).
Root_Cause: Proxy count not configured.
Impact: Brute-force limits can be bypassed.
Verification: Code is ready: one trusted-proxy rule (core/client_ip.py) for throttles, reset limit and audit address; Compose passes the variables; 10 tests (config/tests_hardening_closure.py::ClientIpTests, ProxyAwareThrottleTests) show header rotation no longer resets limits once the count is set. Expected count from the repository is 2 (Traefik + nginx). Not set and not verified on the deployed site.
Residual_Risk: Owner: DevOps. Set API_THROTTLE_NUM_PROXIES and REDIS_URL, then run the checks in KHALSNI_PRODUCTION_ENV_REQUIREMENTS.md section 4.

Title: Only the order total is frozen; other price and name details follow the catalog
Description: Order.final_price is frozen at creation from base + government + service fee. Fee components and the English service name shown on an old order are read live, and a partner's custom price shown in the catalog is not what is frozen.
Reproduction: Create an order, then change the service's fees: the order total stays, the components shown next to it change and no longer add up.
Root_Cause: Partial snapshot.
Impact: Old orders can show a breakdown that disagrees with their total.
Verification: Not changed: which amounts make up the price is an open client decision.
Residual_Risk: Owner: client (decision B10-8), then engineering.

Title: nginx serves media by denylist and sends no security headers for the SPA
Description: Django used an allowlist for public media while nginx denied only two folders, so any other folder under /media/ was public. The SPA, its assets and public media were served without security headers.
Reproduction: Place a file in a new folder under the media volume: nginx serves it. curl -I / shows no CSP, nosniff or frame header.
Root_Cause: Config drift.
Impact: Future uploads could be exposed.
Verification: nginx now returns 404 for every /media/ path except the five public catalog/CMS folders, and sends nosniff, frame, referrer, permissions and content-security-policy headers on what it serves itself. CSP origins were inventoried first (all same-origin). Validated with `nginx -t` and by running the built app behind the real config in a container: frontend/e2e/nginx-deployment.spec.js (2 tests: media allowlist, traversal, headers, and zero CSP violations across visitor, customer, employee and admin screens) plus the full journey through nginx.
Residual_Risk: Not yet deployed. style-src allows inline styles because React sets style attributes.

Title: Several staff actions have no pending state or confirmation; rejection sends a fixed reason
Description: Employee 'approve result and complete' has no confirmation; several submit buttons can be double-clicked; rejection has no reason input.
Reproduction: Double-click 'add note' on the employee page: two notes. Reject an order: the customer always receives the same canned text.
Root_Cause: Forms without submitting state.
Impact: Duplicate notes/manual notifications; uninformative rejection reason. State-changing duplicates are refused by the server.
Verification: Every staff action control is disabled while its request is in flight and a second click is ignored (hooks/useExclusiveAction.js). Completing a request asks for confirmation. Rejection requires a reason typed by the reviewer on the employee and admin pages. Forms keep their content when an action is refused. 6 component tests (EmployeeOrderReviewPage.safety, ProviderOrderDetailsPage.safety) and a browser test (e2e/hardening-closure.spec.js). The server still enforces every transition.

Title: Order wizard maps some server errors to the wrong field; customer order page is Arabic-only
Description: Server document errors are indexed over uploaded files while the UI indexes requirements; unknown error keys are not shown. CustomerOrderDetailsPage has hardcoded Arabic text in English mode.
Reproduction: Skip an optional document and trigger a server error on a later one: the error appears under the wrong field.
Root_Cause: Index mismatch; untranslated page.
Impact: Confusing error placement; mixed-language page in English.
Verification: Customer order details are fully bilingual with no internal identifiers; the order number keeps its direction inside RTL text. Server document errors are matched by document type (new document_errors in the API) or by the documents actually sent, never by position in the requirement list; errors without a visible field appear in the general error area on every step. 12 unit tests (CustomerOrderDetailsPage.test, serviceFormsErrors.test) and a browser test in both languages.
Residual_Risk: Customer-entered notes and catalog names are shown in the language they were written in.

Title: Profile email/phone change needs no re-authentication; reset response time reveals registered addresses
Description: A session token alone could change the login email and the tracking phone. The reset request waited for the mail server only for registered addresses, so response time distinguished them.
Reproduction: Change email via PATCH /api/customer/profile/ with only the access token.
Root_Cause: Design choices.
Impact: Account takeover is easier after a token theft.
Verification: Changing email or phone requires the current password. An email change revokes every earlier token and returns a fresh pair for the current session. Reset emails are sent off the request path so both branches answer alike. 7 tests (config/tests_hardening_closure.py::ProfileIdentityChangeTests, PasswordResetTimingTests).
Residual_Risk: See KHS-043 for what remains. The mobile client must send current_password for these changes.

Title: English-only titles on customer notifications written by code; notification dedupe and list paging reviewed
Description: Rejection, staff-note and completion-recommendation notifications had English-only titles. Dedupe is check-then-create with the key inside a JSON column. Several staff lists are unpaginated.
Reproduction: Read notifications/services.py; request /api/admin/audit-logs/ on a large dataset.
Root_Cause: Design.
Impact: Slow pages at scale; occasional English title in Arabic.
Verification: The three notifications now carry Arabic and English text through the existing localized structure; recommendations skip unpublished services. 3 tests (config/tests_hardening_closure.py::NotificationLanguageTests). Dedupe reviewed: a database rule would need a new column and a clean-up of existing rows, and could fail on production data, so it was not added; workflow events are serialized by the order lock and the PostgreSQL race test shows one notification under concurrent assignment.
Residual_Risk: Paging was not added: no measured need for staff lists, and the public page size is client decision B10-5.

Title: Migration not yet rehearsed on a copy of production PostgreSQL
Description: No production backup was available. The migration was rehearsed on PostgreSQL 16 with data created by the pre-hardening code plus synthetic volume.
Reproduction: See KHALSNI_PRODUCTION_ENV_REQUIREMENTS.md section 5.
Evidence: PostgreSQL 16 rehearsal recorded in KHALSNI_HARDENING_FINAL.md section 5
Root_Cause: No PostgreSQL instance here.
Impact: Backfill duration and locks on production data are untested.
Verification: 20,008 orders: plan clean, migrate 31.7 s, concurrent read+write probe max 64 ms (no blocking), counts and order fingerprint unchanged, 0 orders without a snapshot, rollback to 0014 and forward again clean, complete backend suite green on PostgreSQL.
Residual_Risk: Owner: DevOps. Repeat on a restored production backup before release.

Title: Setting REDIS_URL would break the application: the Redis client library is not installed
Description: Settings switch the cache to Redis when REDIS_URL is set, but backend/requirements.txt did not list the redis package.
Reproduction: Set REDIS_URL and make any throttled request: the cache backend fails to import.
Evidence: pip show redis in the project environment: not found; requirements.txt at base
Root_Cause: Dependency never added.
Impact: The fix recommended for KHS-033 would have taken the site down.
Verification: redis added to requirements. Verified against a redis:7-alpine container: cache set/incr work and 47 login, registration, reset and proxy tests pass with REDIS_URL set.
Residual_Risk: Compose defines no Redis service; one must be added in Coolify.

Title: Staff document preview framed the API download URL with a token in the address
Description: The verification screen put the tokenized API URL in an iframe/img. The API forbids framing and sends files as attachments, so PDF preview could not render, and the token appeared in the address.
Reproduction: Open the document verification screen on a PDF behind the production proxy.
Evidence: frontend/src/pages/employee/EmployeeVerifyDocumentsPage.jsx (base lines 33-43, 135); found by the CSP browser test
Root_Cause: Preview built from a URL instead of the downloaded file.
Impact: Staff could not preview PDFs inline; token exposure in URLs.
Verification: Preview and download use an authorized in-memory download (blob URL). Covered by the CSP browser test on the verification screen.

Title: Residual account-security items
Description: Tokens are kept in web storage. Creating an order overwrites the account's name, phone and national id from the order form without the password. The per-email reset limit (3 per 30 minutes) lets anyone delay a victim's reset.
Reproduction: Read frontend/src/api/client.js; orders/services.py create_customer_order; accounts/password_reset.py.
Root_Cause: Design choices.
Impact: Easier account misuse after a token theft; reset can be delayed by a third party.
Verification: Not changed: each needs a product or architecture decision (what a verified contact is, B10-6; cookie-based sessions).
Residual_Risk: Owner: client for B10-6, then engineering.

Title: First version of the snapshot migration held an exclusive table lock for the whole backfill
Description: As written in the first hardening pass, orders.0015 added the column and rewrote every order in one transaction, so the exclusive lock taken by ALTER TABLE would have blocked all reads and writes on orders until the backfill finished.
Reproduction: Review of the migration before the PostgreSQL rehearsal.
Root_Cause: Schema change and data backfill in one atomic migration.
Impact: Order pages unavailable for the duration of the migration on a large table.
Verification: Split into 0015 (schema only) and 0016 (non-atomic, one commit per 500 orders, re-runnable). PostgreSQL rehearsal with a concurrent read+write probe: max wait 64 ms across 1,717 samples during a 31.7 s migration.
